text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices to make your API easy to use. First, choose clear endpoints that describe the resources, for example /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, such as 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential, because developers need to understand how your API works. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these simple rules helps you build reliable and user-friendly APIs that other developers will enjoy working with.
